headline: SpaceX IPO looms. Funding flows. Defense collaborations abound.
deck: This week, SpaceX's IPO plans dominate while funding rounds and defense partnerships keep the industry buzzing.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. The funding will bolster its capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, tapping into the DoD's increasing appetite for advanced space solutions. This round highlights the defense sector's ongoing commitment to enhancing national security through space.
stories.soWhat: The cash influx indicates that defense priorities are shifting firmly towards space, a trend that could reshape the competitive landscape.

stories.head: SpaceX aims for $75 billion IPO valuation
stories.body: SpaceX is gearing up to raise at least $75 billion in its upcoming IPO, which would value the company at over $1.75 trillion. This ambitious figure comes despite the occasional satellite loss, and it underscores the market's confidence in SpaceX's long-term vision. Investors are clearly betting on Starship's future, even as it remains grounded.
stories.soWhat: If successful, this IPO could redefine capital access in the space sector, but it also raises questions about sustainable valuation in a high-risk industry.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris join forces for SDA bid
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris are collaborating on a tactical Space Development Agency constellation bid, signaling a strategic pooling of resources in defense tech. The partnership aims to leverage each company's strengths in autonomous systems and satellite communications. As the defense sector continues to consolidate, this move could set a precedent for future collaborations.
stories.soWhat: In an environment where competition is fierce, alliances like this may become essential for survival, especially in high-stakes government contracts.

watchlist.title: Watch for SpaceX IPO details next week
watchlist.body: As SpaceX finalizes its IPO plans, investors will be keen to see how its valuation will affect the broader market.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves closer to launch
watchlist.body: With its critical design review cleared, the Dream Chaser's path to operational status could reshape cargo delivery in low Earth orbit.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program suggests ongoing confidence in its ground station capabilities, which may attract further government contracts.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's Series C impacts defense investments
watchlist.body: The success of True Anomaly's funding round could lead to increased investment interest in co-orbital security solutions.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
